assessments.zone: Rural villages of Bongandanga, Pimu, Bosondjo and Boso Mondanda health zones
assessments.evidence: No known armed-group activity in rural Bongandanga territory; state presence comes through secteur administration and police posts, with customary chiefs settling local disputes. Assessed by default without recent sources (web research was unavailable).

assessments.zone: Bongandanga territorial centre and larger towns (>=10,000 people): Ebongo, Ngwele, Boso Magasu, Cite C, Bongandanga, Bososimba, Usine, Yamokole, Bokobala, Boso Modanda
assessments.evidence: Territorial centre and main towns of a Mongala territory with no known armed-group activity; policing, arrests and justice are handled by the PNC and state courts, with possible small FARDC detachments. Not verified against 2025-2026 sources because web research was unavailable.

units.CD4405-bongandanga: Bongandanga territory (Mongala province, south of the Congo river in the Lopori basin) lies far from the eastern and Mai-Ndombe/Kwilu conflict zones and no armed group is known to hold territory in it. Bongandanga centre and the larger settlements of the Pimu, Bosondjo and Boso Mondanda health zones are policed by the Congolese National Police (PNC), with territorial and secteur administration present. Rural villages are assessed as default state (PNC) presence, with customary chiefs settling everyday disputes; security issues are banditry and local land/customary disputes. NOTE: no web research could be done for this unit (search budget exhausted, news sites blocked by the egress proxy), so this assessment rests on general background knowledge, not on 2025-2026 sources, and should be re-checked.
